S88.03.needs: a Cloud account (signed in) in Cloud mode; replies come from the support team, so a reply may not arrive during the test
S88.03.note: The ticket list and ticket screens exist; whether support replies arrive cannot be checked from the code.
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and make sure the app is in Cloud mode.
Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap About.
Tap Contact Support (it only appears for a signed-in Cloud user; Email Support is always there).
Tap New ticket, type a Subject and What happened, then tap Raise ticket.
Open the new ticket from the list, type in Write a reply, tap Send reply.
Compare: the ticket shows in the list with its status, and replies from support appear in the ticket thread.
S88.03.where: Open the side menu > Settings > About > Contact Support > New ticket

S88.04.needs: a Cloud account for the stored-report path; a mail app for Local mode
S88.04.note: In Local mode the mailto link carries only the subject and message, not the build or platform, which differs from Expected.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings.
In the Support group, tap Report App Issue.
Tap the Bug Report chip and type in the box (placeholder: What happened? What did you expect to happen?).
Tap Submit Feedback (Cloud mode) and read the Thank You! alert.
Compare: in Cloud mode the app sends the app version and platform with the report; in Local mode the button reads Email Feedback and opens the mail app.
S88.04.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Report App Issue > Bug Report

S88.05.needs: a Cloud account for server storage; a mail app for Local mode
S88.05.note: The app shows only the confirmation; the team-side storage cannot be checked from the app.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then in the Support group tap Report App Issue.
General Feedback is selected by default; tap it to confirm.
Type a message in the box (placeholder: Tell us what you think...).
Tap Submit Feedback.
Compare: the Thank You! alert appears with Your feedback has been submitted.
S88.05.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Report App Issue > General Feedback

S88.06.needs: a Cloud account for server storage; a mail app for Local mode
S88.06.note: Storage for the team is not visible from the app.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then in the Support group tap Report App Issue.
Tap the Feature Request chip.
Type in the box (placeholder: Describe the feature you would like...).
Tap Submit Feedback.
Compare: the Thank You! alert appears with Your feedback has been submitted.
S88.06.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Report App Issue > Feature Request

S88.07.note: The app has no in-app list of bundle contents; the user sees them only in the .json file in the share sheet. The share sheet sends to any app the user picks, not a built-in support button.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then in the Support group tap Export Diagnostics.
Read the Share diagnostics? alert: it sends app, device and error details, never messages, files or passwords.
Tap Continue; the system share sheet titled Share your AGI diagnostics opens with a .json file.
If the share sheet lets you preview the file, open it to see the fields (app version, platform, locale, time zone, screen size, recent errors); otherwise cancel.
Compare: the Diagnostics exported alert shows a summary, and the user picks the share target in the share sheet.
S88.07.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Support > Export Diagnostics

S88.08.needs: a reply that fails; this cannot be forced reliably from the UI
S88.08.note: The id is shown only when the server logged one; the server side is in apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts and was not traced further.
steps: Open Chat and send a message.
If the reply fails with an error notice, read the text under the reply.
Compare: the notice ends with Reference: followed by an id that the user can quote to support, and it may say Tap to try again.
If no id appears, the server did not log one for that failure.
S88.08.where: Chat > the notice under a reply that failed

S88.16.needs: a Cloud account (the Privacy row sits in the Cloud section of Settings)
S88.16.note: The app only opens a web page; the request form and status tracking live on that web page, which was not checked from the mobile code.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Privacy.
Scroll to the Helpful resources group.
Tap Data rights requests; a web page (/privacy/requests) opens in the browser.
Compare: the web page should let the user submit access, correction or erasure requests and show their status.
S88.16.where: Open the side menu > Settings > Privacy > Helpful resources > Data rights requests

S88.18.needs: a Cloud account for server delivery; in Local mode the report is saved on the device or sent by email
S88.18.note: The MessageBubble.tsx file holds the ellipsis as the escape …, which renders as Report… ; the moderation intake was not traced past services/contentReport.ts.
steps: Send a message in Chat and wait for the AI reply to finish.
Long-press the AI reply.
Tap Report… ; the sheet titled Report this response opens.
Pick a category such as Harmful or dangerous, then type in the box (placeholder: Describe the issue...).
Tap Save report.
Compare: the sheet shows Report submitted for review (or Send this report to AGI? if it was saved on the device).
S88.18.where: Chat > long-press an AI reply > Report…

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

S88.20.needs: a reply that is refused for safety reasons; a Cloud account for server submission
S88.20.note: The notice shows only for refusal finish reasons; in Local mode the appeal goes out through the mail app.
steps: Send a message in Chat that gets a safety refusal (cannot be forced reliably from the UI).
Read the notice: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.
Tap Report on the notice; the screen titled Report an incorrect refusal opens.
Type the reason and tap Submit Feedback (Cloud mode) or Email Feedback (Local mode).
Compare: the Thank You! alert appears and the app goes back.
S88.20.where: Chat > the notice under a reply the model declined for safety reasons > Report
